transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jon Patel (Redwood SE), Lara Nguyen (Ember Tech - Head of Search), Omar Ruiz (Ember Tech - ML Engineer), Priya Shah (Ember Tech - CTO)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we appreciate you carving out time. I'm Maya, AE on the account, with Jon our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Lara: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to chat. Quick agenda — we're trying to understand how Redwood would fit into our reranking pipeline, and what the tradeoffs are between hosted, dedicated, and private.
[00:15] Maya: Perfect. We'll cover integration patterns for vectors, throughput expectations, dimensionality and model options, and then security/compliance. Jon will handle the technical bits.
[00:22] Jon: Hi all. Quick question to start — what's your current stack for retrieval? Are you pure vector DB or hybrid?
[00:28] Omar: We're hybrid. We run Elastic for inverted index and store vectors in Milvus for the embedding stage, then run a reranker that calls a transformer for top-20. Right now QPS peaks around 150-200, p95 latency for rerank is ~400ms, which is ok but costy.
[00:43] Priya: Our goal is to move away from heavy transformer rerank for every query; looking at cheaper embedding-based rerank or smaller models, but we can't lose precision for ecomm search.
[00:52] Jon: Makes sense. A couple of clarifying items: doc count, average doc length, and embedding dimensionality today?
[00:57] Omar: About 50k product docs, avg 150 tokens. Currently using 768-dim vectors from an off-the-shelf model.
[01:05] Jon: Great. So two paths — 1) use Redwood Hosted embeddings + do nearest neighbor lookup in your vector DB (Milvus) then run rerank locally; or 2) use Redwood end-to-end for embeddings + Redwood's rerank service where we handle nearest neighbor and rerank.
[01:21] Lara: If we keep Milvus, how does Redwood integrate? Do you push embedding vectors into our DB or does Redwood call Milvus?
[01:27] Jon: Both patterns are supported. Typically customers push embeddings from our API into their vector DB. You can either generate embeddings via Redwood hosted API and persist to Milvus, or run ingestion in a Redwood Dedicated/private deployment where the embedding generation is co-located to reduce egress and latency. We also support a proxy pattern where Redwood can call your Milvus endpoint if you prefer central control — though that adds network considerations for hosted.
[01:46] Maya: Important call-out: if you care about data residency or need VPC, Dedicated or Private deployments are recommended. Hosted is easiest to start with and we do SOC2, encryption at rest, etc, but we understand regulatory constraints.
[01:56] Lara: Good. On throughput — we peak 200 QPS with spikes. What does Redwood recommend for batching and cost?
[02:02] Jon: For embeddings generation, batching is effective. With Hosted you can hit high throughput by sending batched requests; cost per vector depends on model/dim. For reranking, if you use Redwood's rerank API we optimize KV cache and batching for transformer scoring, and you get lower per-request tails. For 200 QPS, Dedicated reserved pools give predictable throughput with autoscale.
[02:22] Omar: Is there a recommended embedding dimensionality tradeoff? We use 768 now but some vendors push 512 or 384 to save storage.
[02:29] Jon: Right — 768 is common and captures more nuance, 512 and 384 reduce storage and NN cost. We recommend testing: smaller dims can be fine for ecomm if combined with feature engineering or hybrid BM25 signals. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and dimensionality profiles based on your eval set.
[02:46] Priya: Hybrid search — we want to keep BM25 signals for recall and use embeddings for semantic re-rank. Any built-in support for that?
[02:52] Jon: We see that pattern a lot. Most customers do inverted index (Elastic) first, then embed top-k and rerank. Redwood supports structured outputs and you can combine vector scores with BM25 via customizable scoring functions in the rerank stage. If you use our managed pipeline, we can also host a combined scoring layer so you don't need to manage glue code.
[03:10] Lara: What about vector DB vendor lock? If we start pushing vectors to Milvus and later want to move to Pinecone or Weaviate, how painful?
[03:16] Jon: Vector formats are generally portable. Issues are around metadata, namespaces, and runtime glue. We try to avoid lock-in by keeping embeddings as a first-class artifact — you can export vectors. If you want Redwood to manage storage we can also offer a Dedicated-backed store for the pilot.
[03:29] Omar: For latency — our current reranker calls a 2B model; p95 ~400ms but cost is high. If Redwood does smaller model rerank, what's typical p95?
[03:37] Jon: Depends on model. A distilled reranker or optimized LLM at 7B quantized can get p95 under 200ms in Dedicated with batching and prefix caching. Hosted may have slightly higher tails due to multi-tenancy, but we expose performance profiles. We also have automatic fallback to cheaper model variants when load spikes.
[03:52] Maya: Also worth noting the KV cache for session-style reranks reduces repeated context cost, but for single-query rerank it's less relevant.
[03:59] Priya: Security — we need SSO, SAML, audit logs, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys. Do you support that?
[04:06] Maya: Yes. Private deployments include customer-managed KMS/HSM options and VPC peering. Dedicated offers RBAC and longer audit log retention as an add-on. Hosted standard is SOC 2 and encryption at rest, key management by Redwood. We'll share detailed security docs.
[04:21] Lara: How do you handle PII and retention? We want to ensure embeddings aren't stored beyond the ingestion window unless we say so.
[04:28] Jon: We have configurable retention policies. For Hosted, default is short retention but we can set customer-specific contracts for Dedicated/Private. You can also choose not to persist embeddings in Redwood by pushing them directly into Milvus after generation.
[04:40] Omar: Anything we should be worried about with hybrid Elastic + vector DB? Like scoring normalization or tuning?
[04:46] Jon: Score normalization is important. We often normalize BM25 and cosine scores then tune weights via small eval sets. Redwood Optimize can recommend weightings based on your labeled queries.
[04:56] Priya: Pricing — high level? We need to decide between per-token/per-embed hosted vs committed Dedicated.
[05:02] Maya: We'll send a pricing sheet. Hosted is usage-based and easiest to start. Dedicated is commit-based with lower unit cost and SLOs. Private has platform fee. We can model expected costs once you provide QPS and sample sizes.
[05:14] Lara: Ok sounds good. Next steps then — you run a benchmark on our sample set, and we review pricing and deployment options.
[05:20] Maya: Exactly. Jon, can you run the benchmark and include both 768-dim and 512-dim embeddings and a small hybrid rerank test?
[05:27] Jon: Yep. I'll run Hosted tests first to show latency/cost, then we can run a Dedicated run if you'd like.
[05:33] Omar: We'll upload 50k docs and a handful of test queries to the shared S3 link after the call.
[05:37] Priya: Also include a note about network egress and data residency for Hosted — we can't cross certain regions for EU data.
[05:43] Maya: Noted, we'll include region-specific notes and VPC options in the follow-up.
[05:48] Lara: Great. Anything else?
[05:50] Maya: Quick recap: Maya will share pricing + security docs; Jon will run benchmarks (768/512 dims, hybrid rerank) and share spreadsheet; Ember will provide sample data and chosen QPS profile. We'll aim to reconvene after the benchmark.
[06:05] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[06:07] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional speaker overlaps and small transcription errors ("K V cache" instead of KV cache, "dedicate" vs "dedicated").

References mentioned: pricing sheet (link to be shared), security brief (SOC2, VPC, KMS), benchmark script (shared by Jon).
